newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WOOSNAM UNSURE ABOUT HIS FITNESS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOOSNAM UNSURE ABOUT HIS FITNESS.

text.p: Former world number one Ian Woosnam said on Wednesday he had virtually decided to have back surgery, which could keep him out of golf for at least three months.
Just when he faces the prospect of two rounds a day for four days to win his third World Matchplay title this week, Woosnam is wondering if 18 holes a day might be too much for him.

The trouble has spread to his legs and the little Welshman doubts if he has the reserves of stamina he needs to add to his titles at Wentworth in 1987, when he became the first European to win, and 1990.
But he intends to try. Runner-up to Colin Montgomerie for the European Order of Merit this year, Woosnam will face the Scot in the first round of the Matchplay on Friday.

"In the near future I have to make a decision what I'm going to do. I have more or less decided on surgery but it's just a question of when," said Woosnam, who reigned as world number one for 50 weeks after he won the U.S. Masters in 1989.
"I'm thinking long term. I want to play a lot longer but the way I'm going at the moment I don't see much future in trying to play as I am now.

"When you're feeling good and playing free it's okay. Then you get three or four weeks of backache and leg aches and the game's gone again. All of a sudden the posture changes and the swing changes and it's difficult to keep the rhythm.
"When I feel good, I feel a different person. The mind is working right, it's a different ball game.
"But it's hard enough to win these tournaments when you're feeling fit. When you not feeling well all the time, you have no chance."
Woosnam, who has won four tournaments in Europe this year, suffers from spondylosis, a condition affecting the vertebrae. It has troubled him sporadically for many years.
"The doctor might fuse two vertebrae together, take pieces off them or just clean them up. That's what I have to talk to him about.
"He assures me it is fixable and won't stop me playing golf but I'd probably have to take at least three months off."
His condition has improved since he missed the halfway cut at the German Masters two weeks ago.
"Right now I'm hitting the ball well and if I can keep my driving straight I could do all right. But the course is playing long because it is damp," he said.
"There are no sharp pains like before. I can cope with the backache because I can loosen my back up. It's the leg pains that hurt more.
"It can happen walking down the first hole. It's like you're walking up hill all the time and carrying your golf bag. The leg pains make you feel you can't complete 18 holes properly.
"Sometimes you can wake up feeling great. Maybe I will tomorrow but I will definitely need physiotherapy after 18 holes tomorrow. But I have to get on with it, fight through it and battle on."
Woosnam added: "Two weeks ago I thought of asking to have someone on standby in case I couldn't play. Now it feels better but we'll just have to see what happens."
